paragraphs.original: The synthetic imagery of \Cref{sec:synthetic_data_supplementation} came from a single generative model, chosen early on a visual comparison against a few alternatives. That choice is load-bearing. If a cheaper or free model would have served as well, or if apparent realism does not translate into detection accuracy, the conclusions of the synthetic-data experiments change. The second possibility is not hypothetical. Earlier work by the present author found that generated image context conferred no downstream advantage over random noise on a small-object car-detection task \cite{hedrichGeneratingSyntheticDatasets2026}. This section describes the controlled comparison built to test it: what was compared, how it was made fair, and how the generators were judged.

paragraphs.original: The fixed detector trains on each cell's synthetic images and is evaluated on real photographs only (\Cref{sec:evaluation_framework}). The headline measure is mean average precision over the real test set. Per-class average precision separates the data-rich anchors from the rare classes. The within-group confusion rate over the three zebra species, the fraction of correctly localized detections landing in the right look-alike group but the wrong species, is the sharpest available test of whether synthetic data teaches species-level discrimination. Only the zebras have more than one member of a frozen look-alike group (\Cref{sec:lookalike_groups}) here, so the bear group's rate is structurally zero and excluded.

paragraphs.original: The criterion was fixed in advance. A generator counts as usable if it lands within a stated margin of the incumbent on the axes that matter, downstream accuracy on real photographs and diagnostic fidelity, \emph{and} is practical on cost and throughput. Raw photorealism alone is not sufficient, since it is the impression that motivated the original choice. The production choice is justified only if the incumbent sits at or near the top. Because differences on a dataset this small may fall within run-to-run noise, results are reported as a mean with its spread across seeds, and two cells whose intervals overlap are indistinguishable rather than ranked.
